currentCard.explanation: Эритроциты содержат гемоглобин, который обратимо связывает кислород. Благодаря этому они переносят кислород от лёгких к тканям организма.

literal.prompt: Какие элементы крови переносят основную часть кислорода?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 18.3 L30-L31 identifies erythrocytes as the formed element whose main role is carrying inhaled oxygen to tissues; L38/L46-L47 give their hemoglobin binding capacity and pulmonary pickup/tissue release.18.4 assigns platelets hemostasis and lymphocytes/neutrophils immune functions, not principal oxygen carriage. Thus key3 is unique among this actual row. «Основную часть» avoids claiming that no oxygen is dissolved in plasma, and «элементы» accommodates platelet fragments. Four plural blood-element names are comparable without a grammatical clue.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 18.3 L38/L44-L47 places hemoglobin in erythrocytes and explicitly describes oxygen loading in lungs and release at tissues. Reversibility is the faithful mechanism inferred from binding then release, rather than the oxygen being consumed by hemoglobin. The second sentence connects this to lung-to-tissue transport, also explicit L31. Two coherent sentences directly name erythrocytes; no unsupported therapy or exclusive-all-oxygen claim.

absoluteLevel.ground: Erythrocytes/red blood cells carry oxygen is a broad school-level fact familiar to a large adult audience. The player need not know neutrophil subtypes, B/T immunology, a rare number, or a clinical interpretation to identify the red-cell role. The alternatives remain real blood elements of comparable detail, permitting knowledge-based choice rather than eliminating an absurd entity. EASY is an editorial audience assessment, not measured human acceptance.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Erythrocytes contain hemoglobin, whose oxygen binding is reversible.
correctNoteExtraFact.ground: The named intracellular molecule and loading/release mechanism are additional own-erythrocyte facts beyond merely identifying the oxygen-carrying blood element.18.3 L38/L46-L47 directly grounds them; overlap with explanation is permitted.
